title: 6 Park Eun-bin K-dramas to watch after "Spooky in Love" - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong

 By Tom Kao August 21, 2026 With "Spooky in Love" heading into its finale on August 23, you might already be wondering where to get your next Park Eun-bin fix. Luckily, the Korean actress has built an impressively varied filmography, moving effortlessly between heartfelt romances, dark thrillers, historical dramas and even superhero comedy. From her global breakout to some of her most unexpected transformations, here are six Park Eun-bin K-dramas worth watching next 
 Extraordinary Attorney Woo (2022)
 If there is one Park Eun-bin drama everyone should watch, it is Extraordinary Attorney Woo . She stars as Woo Young-woo, a rookie lawyer on the autism spectrum whose 164 IQ, remarkable memory and unconventional thinking help her tackle complex cases at a top law firm. Along the way, she navigates workplace prejudice, new friendships and a sweet romance with colleague Lee Jun-ho. The global hit cemented Park as an international star, with her thoughtful performance earning her the Grand Prize at the 2023 Baeksang Arts Awards.
 Hyper Knife (2025)
 Want to see just how far Park can transform? Hyper Knife takes her to much darker territory as Jung Se-ok, a once-promising neurosurgeon stripped of her medical licence after clashing with mentor Choi Deok-hee (Sul Kyung-gu). Now a pharmacist by day and illegal surgeon by night, Se-ok’s dangerous double life is upended when a terminally ill Deok-hee returns asking her to save him. What follows is a tense battle of revenge and medical obsession, with Park embracing one of her darkest, most unhinged roles yet.
 Castaway Diva (2023)
 Park shows off another side of her talents in Castaway Diva as Seo Mok-ha, an aspiring singer who becomes stranded on a deserted island for 15 years while escaping her abusive father. After being rescued, she reconnects with her fading idol Yoon Ran-joo and secretly sings on her behalf while chasing her own long-delayed dream of stardom. Equal parts uplifting and emotional, the series puts Park’s natural warmth front and centre - and, impressively, she performed Mok-ha’s songs herself.

 Do You Like Brahms? (2020)
 In the mood for something quieter? Do You Like Brahms? sees Park play Chae Song-ah, a business graduate who returns to university to pursue violin despite starting years behind her peers. There, she grows close to acclaimed pianist Park Joon-young (Kim Min-jae), who is dealing with burnout and an unrequited love of his own. As the two find comfort in each other, the gentle slow-burn romance explores ambition, self-doubt and knowing when to let go of a dream. Park even relearned the violin for the role.
 The King’s Affection (2021)
 For a sweeping historical romance, The King’s Affection has Park playing Dam-i, a girl secretly spared after the birth of royal twins who later assumes the identity of her deceased brother, Crown Prince Lee Hwi. Hiding her gender while navigating palace politics is difficult enough, but things get even trickier when her first love Jung Ji-un (Rowoon) returns as her royal tutor. With forbidden romance and the constant threat of discovery, the series gives Park one of her most compelling transformations.
 The Wonderfools (2026)
 Finally, if you want Park at her most chaotic, queue up The Wonderfools . Set in 1999 amid Y2K doomsday panic, she stars alongside Cha Eun-woo as Haeseong troublemaker Eun Chae-ni, who unexpectedly gains superpowers alongside a group of equally unlikely heroes. As mysterious events threaten their city, the misfits must figure out their bizarre new abilities and somehow save the day. Absurd, nostalgic and action-packed, it is a fitting final pick that proves Park is just as comfortable playing an unlikely superhero as she is a lawyer, surgeon or crown prince.
